What we should do is re-examine laws regarding Corporations. In the early days of this fine Republic corporations were not allowed to own property in the form of other businesses or other corporations. Corporations were granted a charter only if there was a specific purpose that benefitted the public. Once that benefit was achieved, the corporation was dissolved.

Example: Let's say you had 2 communities on opposite sides of a river and the only way to get from one side to the other was on a ferry or barge. The communities would benefit if there was a bridge across the river. So, investors would create a corporation with the purpose of building a bridge. The project will work better if there is one business entity to enter into contracts for everything from engineering & design, labor, materials, and anything else that's needed. Once the project is complete and the investors are fairly compensated, the BRIDGE CORPORATION is dissolved.

The real reason we have corporations as we know them today is so the wealthy business owners can avoid liability. If you're a sole proprietor and you make a defective product that causes harm, you will be held accountable. If it's a corporation that's making a defective product that causes harm, the corporation, or rather the shareholders will be held accountable.
